title: Cardinality dependence in submodular maximization with bandit feedback
short_statement: How much does the cardinality budget affect learning a monotone submodular objective from noisy set-value observations? The relevant benchmark here is robust greedy regret, not ordinary approximation regret.
open_problem: Close the cardinality-dependence gap for unrestricted algorithms under the robust-greedy regret benchmark defined above.
background:
With aggregate feedback, a learner sees only a noisy value of the entire selected set. It cannot directly estimate each item's contribution from that observation. This makes the interaction between set size and exploration informative. A benchmark must also account for the difficulty of identifying a particular greedy trajectory when marginal gains are nearly tied.

The earlier description conflated two different comparators. This matters for correctness: an upper bound for a stronger comparator can imply one for a weaker comparator, but a lower bound cannot be transferred in that direction. A purported improvement must therefore first identify the precise objective it controls.
full_statement: Choose $S_t\subseteq[n]$, $|S_t|\le k$, and observe $f(S_t)+\eta_t$, where $f$ is unknown normalized monotone submodular, bounded in $[0,1]$ on feasible sets, and noise is iid mean-zero 1-sub-Gaussian. Define $\mathcal G_\epsilon$ as size-$k$ sets admitting a chain $S_0=\varnothing\subset\cdots\subset S_k$ with $$\max_{a\notin S_{i-1}}f(S_{i-1}\cup\{a\})-f(S_i)\le\epsilon_i.$$ The benchmark is $$R_{\rm gr}=\min_{\epsilon\ge0,\,S\in\mathcal G_\epsilon}\left[T f(S)+T\sum_{i=1}^k\epsilon_i-\sum_{t=1}^T f(S_t)\right].$$ Determine $\inf_A\sup_f\mathbb E R_{\rm gr}$, particularly its cardinality dependence. The known lower and upper bound summaries differ in the factors $L^{1/3}$ and $L$ multiplying $n^{1/3}T^{2/3}$, respectively, after minimizing over $0\le L\le k$ with the additional term $\sqrt{\binom n{k-L}T}$. Exact parameter regimes are in Theorems 2.1 and 2.3 of the source.
known_results:
Tajdini, Jain, and Jamieson analyze $R_{\rm gr}$ (Section 1.1, equation 3), which upper-bounds $(1-1/e)$-approximation regret. Their lower bound does not thereby become a lower bound for the latter. The stronger cardinality lower bound assumes nonadaptive greedy-error thresholds; Sub-UCB attains the corresponding upper bound.

Zhou, Gaillard, Rahier, and Arbel (ALT 2025) study unconstrained nonmonotone functions with a $1/2$ comparator. Nie, Aggarwal, and Quinn study multi-label $k$-submodularity; that $k$ is not this cardinality budget. Neither result directly settles this entry.

progress.summary: Benchmark corrected on 2026-11-09. No closure of this exact gap was located in the targeted search; this is not an exhaustive current-status certification.

counterexample_rationale: This is a minimax regret rate question (an asymptotic scaling gap between a proven lower bound and an achieved upper bound), not an existence/nonexistence question, so it cannot be resolved by a single explicit finite counterexample; progress requires either a sharper information-theoretic lower-bound argument or a new algorithm with matching analysis.
alphaevolve_rationale: Closing a minimax regret exponent gap is fundamentally an analytical/information-theoretic task (constructing hard instance families for lower bounds, or designing and analyzing new estimators/algorithms for upper bounds) rather than a search over discrete combinatorial constructions or numeric constants, so an evolutionary code-search loop is a poor fit; it could conceivably help empirically benchmark candidate algorithms' regret on synthetic submodular instances, but that would not constitute a proof of the tight rate.

literature.synthesis: Compare results only after matching the feedback, feasible sets, comparator, and algorithm restrictions. Adjacent pure-exploration, unconstrained, and multi-label results should not be advertised as closing this gap.

reviewed.ref: Guanyu Nie, Vaneet Aggarwal, Christopher John Quinn, Stochastic k-Submodular Bandits with Full Bandit Feedback, AAMAS 2025 extended abstract
reviewed.result: Multiple assignment labels and several constraint families, not a closure of this cardinality gap.

agent_guidance.suitable_approaches: Test whether data-dependent exploration thresholds improve the tradeoff. Alternatively construct a lower bound against unrestricted adaptive rules.
agent_guidance.verification_notes: Do not replace robust greedy regret by approximation regret. State all restrictions on n, k, T, the noise distribution and the algorithm class. The source's theorem-level lower bounds have parameter restrictions beyond the compact abstract summary. Empirical performance is not an asymptotic minimax proof.

where_posed.text: Gap between the unrestricted lower bound and Sub-UCB upper bound in Tajdini, Jain, and Jamieson.
